context: Both heaps are complete binary trees with 12 nodes. The first three levels are full, and the fourth has 5 consecutive nodes starting at the far left. The table lists the values level by level from top to bottom, reading each level from left to right. The level numbers come from these positions and do not appear in the figure.
description: Both trees have the same connections. Each root has two children, as does each node on the second level. From left to right on the third level, the first two nodes each have two children, the third has only a left child, and the fourth is a leaf. Together with the table, this identifies every parent-child connection.

frames.explanation: The labels below the trees give the ordering rules. In a min-heap, each parent's value is less than or equal to each child's. In a max-heap, it is greater than or equal to each child's. Equal values are allowed. For example, the right node on the second level of the min-heap and its left child both have value 2. Nodes on one level need not be sorted from left to right, and siblings can appear in either order.
frames.title: Structure and ordering of min-heaps and max-heaps

result: Comparing each parent with its children level by level shows that the min-heap's root, 1, is the minimum value in its heap, and the max-heap's root, 9, is the maximum in its heap.
summary: The min-heap on the left and the max-heap on the right have the same shape, with opposite ordering rules for parents and children.
